indicator_definition: This indicator measures the number of researchers in full-time equivalents (FTE) per million inhabitants. Researchers are professionals engaged in creating new knowledge, products, processes and systems. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national R&D statistics.
rationale: Researchers are a key input to the innovation process. A larger research workforce drives scientific progress and economic competitiveness. Progress means an increasing number of researchers per million inhabitants across all sectors of the economy.
methodology_characteristics: Data are compiled by Eurostat from R&D surveys following the OECD Frascati Manual. Researchers are counted in full-time equivalents to account for part-time work. Data cover business enterprise, government, higher education and private non-profit sectors.
indicator_name: Researchers in full-time equivalents per million inhabitants
